soundness_flags.label: def:predictable-class and def:frontier-rate
soundness_flags.one_line: The class places no conditional scale bound on the arm means or on the IPW score, so its normalized rate b_nm omits a load-bearing variance/SNR quantity: sub-Gaussian innovations alone do not control assignment noise from arbitrary μ0,μ1.

soundness_flags.label: thm:ipw-rowwise-upper
soundness_flags.one_line: Even in the constant-propensity submodel with n=m, r=μ=K=1, bounded nonzero common arm means, and σr(M) at the stated √(n log n) gap, IPW assignment noise projected onto V has maximum-row subspace error of constant normalized order, not O_P(b_nm)=O_P(n^(-1/2)).

soundness_flags.label: lem:blind-expansion and prop:constant-propensity-reduction
soundness_flags.one_line: At constant propensities, replacing p̄i by p̂i creates a row-common denominator fluctuation whose tangent component is generally first order at the stated signal gap; it is not uniformly o_P(b_nm), so blind and recorded SVDs need not share the claimed first-order expansion.

soundness_flags.label: ass:innovation-centering
soundness_flags.one_line: This is an immediate consequence of the definition μa_ij=E[Yij(a)|F_i,j-1] and should not be retained as an independent class condition.

soundness_flags.label: ass:subgaussian-innovations
soundness_flags.one_line: Tropp2011Freedman does not support the tagged conditional ψ2 assumption: its matrix Freedman theorem assumes a uniform almost-sure bound on martingale differences plus predictable quadratic variation.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Matrix Freedman assumes uniformly bounded self-adjoint differences λmax(Xk)≤R (or rectangular differences ||Xk||≤R) and uses predictable quadratic variation; it does not state a conditional Orlicz-ψ2 increment assumption.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Rebuild the constant-propensity calculation first: add a primitive conditional scale condition for both arm means/IPW scores and derive a rate retaining its necessary σr(M), row-maximum, and logarithmic dependence before claiming an adaptive extension.

Treat empirical row normalization as a separate leading tangent term; either include that term in the blind frontier or impose and justify a signal regime strong enough to make it negligible, then re-check the constant-propensity reduction.

Remove ass:innovation-centering as definitional and replace the Tropp citation with a source that actually supports conditional sub-Gaussian martingale increments, or change the tail assumption to Tropp's bounded-increment form.

recommended_next_step: Reject this version and return to Stage -1 to recalibrate the fixed-propensity SNR and blind-denominator expansions before any Stage-0 proof work.
